FRETBOARD HERO / DAILY ROUTINE

Give your next practice session a direction.

Daily Routine brings five exercises together in one key. Work through note finding, a scale, triads, rhythm and pentatonic movement at your own pace.

Try this exercise ↗

Written by Jean-François Seignemorte · Reviewed 27 October 2026

Five exercises, one musical context

The free routine starts in A minor. Keeping one key throughout the session helps you recognize the same notes in different exercises.

  • Find the root notes: locate the tonal anchor on the neck.
  • Play a scale: follow the displayed note sequence.
  • Connect triads: recognize small chord shapes and their notes.
  • Practice rhythm: listen to a strumming pattern and play it back.
  • Explore pentatonic movement: connect notes across positions.

Try a ten-minute session

Ten minutes is a suggested practice format, not a timer imposed by the app. Spend about two minutes on each exercise, or stay longer on the one that needs attention.

  1. Tune your guitar, open Daily Routine and begin with A minor.
  2. Follow each tablature slowly enough to hear clean notes. Repeat a short section when it feels uncertain.
  3. For rhythm, listen to the example and choose a comfortable tempo. Scale and pentatonic note-following exercises do not require a fixed BPM.
  4. Finish by replaying one phrase without looking at the screen.

Choose microphone feedback or manual practice

Supported exercises can follow your playing through the microphone. Grant permission when you want to use it, and keep background sound low. The tuner and live feedback process audio on your device.

You can turn the microphone off and move through the routine manually. The app cannot judge every aspect of technique, tone or musical expression; listening to yourself and getting feedback from a teacher are still useful.

Questions before you start

Do I have to complete every exercise?

You can work at your own pace, repeat a section and move to the next exercise manually.

Does every exercise use the rhythm tempo?

No. The BPM setting belongs to rhythm practice. Note-following scale and pentatonic exercises are not a metronome test.

What if microphone access does not work?

Check browser support and permissions. You can continue with visual guidance and manual completion even when live microphone feedback is unavailable.

Start with the free demo

The demo lets you explore the key of A, with an A minor Daily Routine and the note A on the Fretboard Map. The Android app offers a one-time in-app purchase, with no subscription. Check the app for the current price and purchase terms.

Open the app

Try the web app in your browser or use the Android app. Microphone feedback depends on your browser, device and permission; you can also practice without it. An iOS App Store release is not yet linked from this site.
